chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Nasr ibn Is'haq, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Nu'man, from Al-Haytham ibn Hammad, from Abu Dawud, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no servant in my community who is kind to his brother regarding Allah with anything from kindness, except that Allah would have him served by the servants of Paradise.'

key_terms.أَخَاهُ فِي اللَّهِ: His brother in the sake of Allah (fellow believer)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for being kind to a fellow believer for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the spiritual merit of *lutf* (gentleness) in social interactions among believers, framing kindness as an act of worship done purely for Allah's sake. The promise of being served by the inhabitants of Paradise underscores the reciprocal nature of divine grace and the elevated status of those who maintain strong communal bonds (*mu'akhah*). This reflects the Shia emphasis on social piety as a tangible manifestation of faith.
